origins: Some of us grew up with parents who were distant, harsh, absent, addicted, or simply unable to show love in a way we could feel. Children draw their conclusions from what they experience, and a child who did not feel loved often decides, “I was unlovable,” or “they never loved me.” That conclusion can then shape friendships, marriage, and even how we imagine God.
teaches: Scripture is honest that parents can fail. The psalmist says, “Though my father and mother forsake me, the LORD will receive me.” God is called “a father of the fatherless,” and “God settles the lonely in families.” Jeremiah records God’s words, “I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have drawn you with loving devotion.” John says, “Behold what manner of love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God. And that is what we are!” Even if human love fell short, God’s love for you is not in question. A parent’s failure to show love is a real wound, but it is not a verdict on your worth.
self_statements: There must be something wrong with me or they would have loved me.
No one will ever love me the way a parent should.
I do not matter to the people who should care most.
errors: Feeling unloved and concluding that I was and am unlovable.
Believing their failure to love was caused by something wrong in me.
Seeing parents as either fully loving or never loving at all.
Letting one painful relationship define all love.
questions: What did I actually experience from my parents, and what conclusions did I draw as a child?
Were there any moments, however small, when I was cared for?
What might have been going on in my parents that kept them from loving well?
Is a parent’s inability to love the same as my being unlovable?
What does God say about how He sees me?
Who in my life now shows me love?
truth: My parents’ failure to love me well was real and painful, but it does not define my worth. God has loved me with an everlasting love, and He receives me as His child. I can grieve what I missed and receive what God and His people offer now.
hw_truths: My worth is not decided by how my parents treated me.
God has loved me with an everlasting love.
God settles the lonely in families.
I am a child of God.
log: Each day, write one way you received love or kindness from God or from another person.
actions: Describe what you experienced and what you concluded as a child. Pray over it.
Allow sadness for what you did not receive, with a trusted listener if possible.
List three people or communities who care for you now.
Say it each morning for a week.
prayer: Father, You see the places where I did not feel loved. Receive me, heal what was hurt, and let me know that I am Your child. Bring people into my life who show Your love. Amen.
hw_questions: What did I experience from my parents?
What conclusions did I draw as a child?
What does God say about me?
What do I need to grieve?
Who can I talk with about this?
name_example: Sarah can write: “Even if my parents failed me, the Lord receives me.”
